citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with
its metric-selected connection $\nabla$. A smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K_{ab}$ is a **rank-two Killing tensor** when

$$\nabla_{(a}K_{bc)}:=\frac13\left(\nabla_aK_{bc}+\nabla_bK_{ca}+\nabla_cK_{ab}\right)=0.$$

For a smooth curve $\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ with open interval domain and affine
parameter $\lambda$, write $v=\dot\gamma$. If $\nabla_vv=0$, the curve is an
affinely parametrized geodesic, and $K_{ab}v^av^b$ is its associated quadratic
geodesic integral. It is called **reducible** if it is a finite constant
linear combination of $g_{ab}$ and symmetric products
$\xi^\flat\odot\eta^\flat$, where $\xi,\eta$ are Killing fields,
$\xi^\flat:=g(\xi,\cdot)$, and
$\alpha\odot\beta:=(\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha)/2$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary with affine connection $\nabla$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior. A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ is an **affinely parametrized geodesic** when
$$D_t\gamma'(t)=0\qquad(t\in I),$$
with one-sided interpretation at an included endpoint. Constant curves are geodesics. Unless another parametrization is explicitly stated, “geodesic” means affinely parametrized geodesic.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex (Intervals of $\mathbb{R}$: the nine order-convex forms, nondegeneracy, and length) and let
$f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$ (Continuity of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point of $A$ and on $A$: the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, its agreement with $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ at a limit point, and continuity at an isolated point) and
differentiable at every point of $I$ that is interior to $I$
(Interior, closure, boundary and exterior of a subset of $\mathbb{R}$, The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set), with

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

Then $f$ is constant on $I$: there is a real $k$ with $f(x) = k$ for every
$x \in I$.

Consequently, if $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are both continuous on $I$ and both
differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

$$f(x) \;=\; g(x) + k \qquad \text{for every } x \in I .$$

**Order-convexity of $I$ is essential and is not a convenience.** The
conclusion is false on a domain that falls into separate pieces, since a
function may be constant on each piece with different constants; nothing in the
proof would survive, because the mean value theorem is applied to the segment
joining two points of the domain and that segment must lie in the domain.

**The hypothesis is imposed only at interior points.** At an endpoint of $I$
nothing is asked at all: $f$ need not be differentiable there, and the proof
never evaluates a difference quotient at an endpoint, since it applies the mean
value theorem on a segment $[u,v] \subseteq I$ and uses the derivative only at
points of $(u,v)$, all of which are interior to $I$. What is *not* meant is that
the derivative at an endpoint is free to be nonzero: once $f$ is known to be
constant its difference quotient at an endpoint is constantly $0$, so wherever
$f'$ exists at an endpoint it is $0$ too. That is a consequence of the theorem,
not a hypothesis of it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Define $I_K(\lambda):=K_{ab}(\gamma(\lambda))v^a(\lambda)v^b(\lambda)$. The product rule in [F3] gives $I_K'=(\nabla_vK)(v,v)+2K(D_\lambda v,v)$.

By [F2], $D_\lambda v=0$. Also $v^av^bv^c$ is symmetric in its indices, so $(
abla_vK)(v,v)=v^av^bv^c
abla_aK_{bc} =v^av^bv^c
abla_{(a}K_{bc)}=0$ by [F1]. Thus $I_K'=0$ on $I$.
Apply [F4] to $I_K$ on the connected interval $I$. Therefore $K_{ab}v^av^b$ is constant along $\gamma$.

boundaries.reason: The statement assumes a connected open interval I and an affine geodesic on it.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 uses no nonzero condition on K or v; K=0 gives the constant zero integral.

boundaries.reason: No finite cardinality case is involved.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 never inverts K and remains valid for degenerate or zero Killing tensors.

boundaries.reason: I is open and the conclusion concerns constancy on I, not values at boundary endpoints.
The pointwise differentiation proof selects no element from a nonempty family.
The proposition is a one-way conservation implication.
No converse from a conserved quadratic form to the Killing equation is claimed.

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex (Intervals of $\mathbb{R}$: the nine order-convex forms, nondegeneracy, and length) and let
$f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$ (Continuity of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point of $A$ and on $A$: the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, its agreement with $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ at a limit point, and continuity at an isolated point) and
differentiable at every point of $I$ that is interior to $I$
(Interior, closure, boundary and exterior of a subset of $\mathbb{R}$, The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set), with

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

Then $f$ is constant on $I$: there is a real $k$ with $f(x) = k$ for every
$x \in I$.

Consequently, if $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are both continuous on $I$ and both
differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

$$f(x) \;=\; g(x) + k \qquad \text{for every } x \in I .$$

**Order-convexity of $I$ is essential and is not a convenience.** The
conclusion is false on a domain that falls into separate pieces, since a
function may be constant on each piece with different constants; nothing in the
proof would survive, because the mean value theorem is applied to the segment
joining two points of the domain and that segment must lie in the domain.

**The hypothesis is imposed only at interior points.** At an endpoint of $I$
nothing is asked at all: $f$ need not be differentiable there, and the proof
never evaluates a difference quotient at an endpoint, since it applies the mean
value theorem on a segment $[u,v] \subseteq I$ and uses the derivative only at
points of $(u,v)$, all of which are interior to $I$. What is *not* meant is that
the derivative at an endpoint is free to be nonzero: once $f$ is known to be
constant its difference quotient at an endpoint is constantly $0$, so wherever
$f'$ exists at an endpoint it is $0$ too. That is a consequence of the theorem,
not a hypothesis of it.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

For a covariant $k$-tensor $T=T_{i_1\cdots i_k}dx^{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes dx^{i_k}$, $$ (\mathcal L_XT)_{i_1\cdots i_k}=X^j\partial_jT_{i_1\cdots i_k}+\sum_a(\partial_{i_a}X^j)T_{i_1\cdots j\cdots i_k}. $$

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle and time-orientation conventions of the Lorentzian suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. A **closed spacelike two-surface** is a nonempty smooth embedded two-manifold $S\subset M$ that is compact without boundary. Let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion and let its induced metric be $q:=\iota^*g$; require $q$ to be positive definite. Its normal bundle is $\mathcal NS=(TS)^\perp$. Work on an open set $U\subseteq S$ carrying a smooth ordered pair of future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with $g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-2$; such pairs exist locally by the preceding lemma. No global pair is part of the definition unless one is explicitly supplied.

For tangent fields $X,Y$ on $U$, define the null second fundamental form, expansion and shear by
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y),\qquad \theta_\ell:=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell,\qquad \sigma_\ell:=\chi_\ell-\frac{\theta_\ell}{2}q.$$
Here $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection; its derivative of a section along $S$ means the pullback connection, equivalently the derivative of any smooth ambient extension along tangent directions. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. A **normal-frame boost** is the change $\ell\mapsto e^f\ell$, $k\mapsto e^{-f}k$ for a smooth real function $f$ on $U$. It leaves $q$ fixed; $\chi_\ell,\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$ scale by $e^f$.

A **null geodesic hypersurface congruence from $U$** is a smooth map $F:U\times J\to M$, for an interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$, such that $F(p,0)=p$, every curve $\lambda\mapsto F(p,\lambda)$ is future-directed, null and affinely parametrized, and each map $F_\lambda:=F(\cdot,\lambda)$ is a spacelike immersion before its first focal instant. The field $\ell:=\partial_\lambda F$ is normal to each section and tangent to the immersed null hypersurface swept out by the curves. The parameter $\lambda$ is an affine parameter. On each section, the **screen** is $\mathscr S=\ell^\perp/\mathbb R\ell$ with metric $\bar q([X],[Y])=g(X,Y)$; it is the positive two-dimensional quotient, identified with the tangent plane of that section. The induced form on the full null hypersurface has radical $\mathbb R\ell$ and has no inverse. All traces and inverses in this definition are taken on the screen.

Before the first **focal instant**, the screen Jacobi map $A_\lambda:T_pS\to\mathscr S_{F(p,\lambda)}$ sends $X$ to the screen class of the variation field $J_X(\lambda):=dF_{(p,\lambda)}(X,0)$ and is invertible. The first focal instant is the first positive $\lambda$ at which $A_\lambda$ loses rank. Along an affine generator the screen derivative is $\mathcal D_\ell[X]:=[D_\ell X]$; it is independent of the representative, by the preceding lemma. The derivative $A_\lambda'$ is taken using $\mathcal D_\ell$. The **optical endomorphism** is $B_\lambda:=A_\lambda'A_\lambda^{-1}$, the **optical expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}B$, and the **optical shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\,\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S}$. Since the congruence is normal to a null hypersurface, $B$ is self-adjoint; equivalently its twist vanishes. At $\lambda=0$, $B$ is the endomorphism $q^{-1}\chi_\ell$ and these optical quantities agree with $\theta_\ell,\sigma_\ell$.

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**The scope is exactly the continuous case, and that is not a limitation of the
proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

For $a>0$, the function $x\mapsto a^x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and
$$(a^x)'=a^x\log a.$$
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, with
$$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}.$$

Let $k\in\mathbb N$. Finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps is $C^k$. Scalar multiples are included among the finite componentwise operations. The assertions remain valid on an empty open domain.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The coefficients in [F1] have no $t$ or $\phi$ dependence. For $T=\partial_t$ and $\Phi=\partial_\phi$, the coordinate components are constant, so every term in [F4] vanishes; hence $\mathcal L_Tg=\mathcal L_\Phi g=0$ and both fields are Killing by [F3].

Choose $0<\varepsilon<r_+/2$ and use the extension manifold $\mathbb R_v\times(r_+-\varepsilon,\infty)\times S^2$ with its product smooth structure, round metric $\gamma$, and global axial one-form $\eta$. Fix $r_0>r_+$ and define $f(r)=\int_{r_0}^r (s^2+a^2)/\Delta(s)\,ds$ and $h(r)=\int_{r_0}^r a/\Delta(s)\,ds$ on $(r_+,\infty)$. Their integrands are smooth because $\Delta>0$: repeated use of [F7] gives all derivatives of $\Delta^{-1}$, and [F8] handles the polynomial products. [F6] gives $f,h\in C^1$, and successive differentiation of $f'=(r^2+a^2)/\Delta$ and $h'=a/\Delta$ shows that both primitives are smooth. Set $v=t+f(r)$ and $\widetilde\phi=\phi+h(r)$; globally the sphere coordinate is rotated by the smooth rotation $R_{h(r)}(x,y,z)=(x\cos h-y\sin h,x\sin h+y\cos h,z)$, whose inverse uses $-h(r)$. Repeated application of [F10] makes sine and cosine smooth, and [F8] then makes this rotation smoothly dependent on $r$. Thus this is a smooth coordinate change on the exterior (with coordinate Jacobian determinant $1$), and on an off-axis chart $\eta=\sin^2\theta\,d\widetilde\phi$, while the original $\xi^\flat=\eta-a\sin^2\theta\,\Delta^{-1}dr$. The rotation is generated by $\xi$, so $\eta$ is the standard smooth axial one-form on the new sphere factor. Substitution in [F1], using $\Sigma^2+a^2\sin^2\theta(\Sigma+2Mr)=(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta$, gives the global ingoing expression $g=-(\Delta-a^2|\xi|_\gamma^2)\Sigma^{-1}dv\otimes dv+dv\otimes dr+dr\otimes dv+\Sigma\gamma+a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)\Sigma^{-1}\eta\otimes\eta-2aMr\Sigma^{-1}(dv\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dv)-a(dr\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dr)$. Every coefficient is smooth at $r=r_+$ because $\Sigma>0$ there and no coefficient contains $\Delta$ in a denominator. Off the axis the determinant is $-\Sigma^2\sin^2\theta$. Off the axis the angular $2\times2$ block is positive definite; the determinant of its $2\times2$ Schur complement in the $(v,r)$ directions is therefore negative, giving one negative and one positive eigenvalue. At an axis point $\eta=0$ and $\Sigma=r^2+a^2$; the $(v,r)$ block has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-\Delta/\Sigma&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ of determinant $-1$, and the sphere block is $\Sigma\gamma$, so the extension is Lorentzian there as well. It is consequently a smooth Lorentzian extension across $r=r_+$. In this chart $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=\Delta/\Sigma$, so $dr(\sharp_g dr)=g^{-1}(dr,dr)=0$ on $H^+$ by [F9]; the normal is null and tangent there.

Put $A=r^2+a^2$. In the ingoing chart the inverse metric has $g^{vr}=A/\Sigma$, $g^{\widetilde\phi r}=a/\Sigma$, and $g^{rr}=\Delta/\Sigma$. Thus on $H^+$, $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)\partial_v+(a/\Sigma)\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$ by [F9]. The stationary and axial fields remain $\partial_v$ and $\partial_{\widetilde\phi}$, so $\sharp_g(dr)=(A/\Sigma)(T+(a/A)\Phi)$. It follows that the null normal direction is $\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$ with $\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. Equivalently, $\Delta(r_+)=0$ gives $2Mr_+=r_+^2+a^2$, and direct substitution yields $g(\chi,\chi)|_{r_+}=0$.

From [F1], $g(T,T)=-(1-2Mr/\Sigma)$. It is positive precisely when $r^2-2Mr+a^2\cos^2\theta<0$. The two roots of this quadratic in $r$ are $M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}$; because $|a|<M$, they are real, and the upper root is $r_{\mathrm s}(\theta)$. Restricting to the exterior gives $r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta)$. At $\theta=0,\pi$ the upper root equals $r_+$; for $0<\theta<\pi$ it exceeds $r_+$. This proves the stated ergoregion condition.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth tangent-bundle and time-orientation conventions of the Lorentzian suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. A **closed spacelike two-surface** is a nonempty smooth embedded two-manifold $S\subset M$ that is compact without boundary. Let $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion and let its induced metric be $q:=\iota^*g$; require $q$ to be positive definite. Its normal bundle is $\mathcal NS=(TS)^\perp$. Work on an open set $U\subseteq S$ carrying a smooth ordered pair of future null normal fields $\ell,k$ with $g(\ell,\ell)=g(k,k)=0$ and $g(\ell,k)=-2$; such pairs exist locally by the preceding lemma. No global pair is part of the definition unless one is explicitly supplied.

For tangent fields $X,Y$ on $U$, define the null second fundamental form, expansion and shear by
$$\chi_\ell(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\ell,Y),\qquad \theta_\ell:=\operatorname{tr}_q\chi_\ell,\qquad \sigma_\ell:=\chi_\ell-\frac{\theta_\ell}{2}q.$$
Here $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection; its derivative of a section along $S$ means the pullback connection, equivalently the derivative of any smooth ambient extension along tangent directions. The preceding lemma establishes extension independence, symmetry of $\chi_\ell$, and positive definiteness of the screen metric. supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**The scope is exactly the continuous case, and that is not a limitation of the
proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

supplier_excerpts.consumer_use: 2.1: Choose $0<\varepsilon<r_+/2$ and use the extension manifold $\mathbb R_v\times(r_+-\varepsilon,\infty)\times S^2$ with its product smooth structure, round metric $\gamma$, and global axial one-form $\eta$. Fix $r_0>r_+$ and define $f(r)=\int_{r_0}^r (s^2+a^2)/\Delta(s)\,ds$ and $h(r)=\int_{r_0}^r a/\Delta(s)\,ds$ on $(r_+,\infty)$. Their integrands are smooth because $\Delta>0$: repeated use of [F7] gives all derivatives of $\Delta^{-1}$, and [F8] handles the polynomial products. [F6] gives $f,h\in C^1$, and successive differentiation of $f'=(r^2+a^2)/\Delta$ and $h'=a/\Delta$ shows that both primitives are smooth. Set $v=t+f(r)$ and $\widetilde\phi=\phi+h(r)$; globally the sphere coordinate is rotated by the smooth rotation $R_{h(r)}(x,y,z)=(x\cos h-y\sin h,x\sin h+y\cos h,z)$, whose inverse uses $-h(r)$. Repeated application of [F10] makes sine and cosine smooth, and [F8] then makes this rotation smoothly dependent on $r$. Thus this is a smooth coordinate change on the exterior (with coordinate Jacobian determinant $1$), and on an off-axis chart $\eta=\sin^2\theta\,d\widetilde\phi$, while the original $\xi^\flat=\eta-a\sin^2\theta\,\Delta^{-1}dr$. The rotation is generated by $\xi$, so $\eta$ is the standard smooth axial one-form on the new sphere factor. Substitution in [F1], using $\Sigma^2+a^2\sin^2\theta(\Sigma+2Mr)=(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta$, gives the global ingoing expression $g=-(\Delta-a^2|\xi|_\gamma^2)\Sigma^{-1}dv\otimes dv+dv\otimes dr+dr\otimes dv+\Sigma\gamma+a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)\Sigma^{-1}\eta\otimes\eta-2aMr\Sigma^{-1}(dv\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dv)-a(dr\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes dr)$. Every coefficient is smooth at $r=r_+$ because $\Sigma>0$ there and no coefficient contains $\Delta$ in a denominator. Off the axis the determinant is $-\Sigma^2\sin^2\theta$. Off the axis the angular $2\times2$ block is positive definite; the determinant of its $2\times2$ Schur complement in the $(v,r)$ directions is therefore negative, giving one negative and one positive eigenvalue. At an axis point $\eta=0$ and $\Sigma=r^2+a^2$; the $(v,r)$ block has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-\Delta/\Sigma&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ of determinant $-1$, and the sphere block is $\Sigma\gamma$, so the extension is Lorentzian there as well. It is consequently a smooth Lorentzian extension across $r=r_+$. In this chart $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=\Delta/\Sigma$, so $dr(\sharp_g dr)=g^{-1}(dr,dr)=0$ on $H^+$ by [F9]; the normal is null and tangent there.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose

derivations.claim: Work first on a polar chart with $0<\theta<\pi$ and change angular coordinate to $u=\cos\theta$. Put $q=1-u^2$, $S=r^2+a^2u^2$, $D=r^2-2Mr+a^2$, and $A=r^2+a^2$. In coordinate order $(t,\phi,r,u)$ the metric is block diagonal between $(t,\phi)$ and $(r,u)$: $g=G\oplus h$, where $G=S^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}2Mr-S&-2Marq\\-2Marq&q(A^2-a^2Dq)\end{pmatrix}$ and $h=\operatorname{diag}(S/D,S/q)$. Direct $2\times2$ inversion gives $G^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}-(A^2-a^2Dq)/(SD)&-2Mar/(SD)\\-2Mar/(SD)&(D-a^2q)/(SDq)\end{pmatrix}$, with $\det G=-Dq$; the inverse base block is $h^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(D/S,q/S)$.

The derivatives needed below are $S_r=2r$, $S_u=2a^2u$, $S_{rr}=2$, $S_{ru}=0$, $S_{uu}=2a^2$, $D_r=2(r-M)$, $D_{rr}=2$, $q_u=-2u$, and $q_{uu}=-2$. On this chart $S,D,q>0$, so every denominator in the metric and inverse block is nonzero.

Write Greek indices $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ for $t,\phi$ and Latin indices $i,j,k,\ell$ for $r,u$. Since $G,h$ are independent of $t,\phi$, the complete nonzero Christoffel families from [F3] are $$\Gamma^\alpha{}_{\beta i}=\Gamma^\alpha{}_{i\beta}=\frac12(G^{-1})^{\alpha\gamma}\partial_iG_{\gamma\beta},\qquad \Gamma^i{}_{\alpha\beta}=-\frac12(h^{-1})^{ij}\partial_jG_{\alpha\beta},\qquad \Gamma^i{}_{jk}=\frac12(h^{-1})^{i\ell}(\partial_jh_{\ell k}+\partial_kh_{\ell j}-\partial_\ell h_{jk});$$ all families not forced by lower-index symmetry vanish. The six base coefficients, making the last family explicit, are $$\Gamma^r{}_{rr}=\frac rS-\frac{r-M}{D},\quad \Gamma^r{}_{ru}=\frac{a^2u}{S},\quad \Gamma^r{}_{uu}=-\frac{Dr}{Sq},\quad \Gamma^u{}_{rr}=-\frac{a^2uq}{SD},\quad \Gamma^u{}_{ru}=\frac rS,\quad \Gamma^u{}_{uu}=\frac{a^2u}{S}+\frac uq.$$ Thus the first two matrix families are fully specified by the displayed $G,G^{-1},h^{-1}$ and their $r,u$ derivatives, rather than by omitted connection coefficients.

Put $W_r:=(r-M)/D$, $W_u:=-u/q$, and $P_i:=G^{-1}\partial_iG$. The determinant identity $\partial_i\det G=(\det G)\operatorname{tr}(G^{-1}\partial_iG)$ and $\det G=-Dq$ give $\Gamma^\alpha{}_{\alpha i}=W_i$ after summing $\alpha$. Also $\sqrt{|\det G\det h|}=S$. In the $\alpha\beta$ contraction, $\partial_i\Gamma^i{}_{\alpha\beta}+\Gamma^c{}_{ci}\Gamma^i{}_{\alpha\beta}$ combines to the displayed divergence term, while the two mixed-block quadratic-Christoffel terms combine to the displayed matrix product. The $ij$ contraction leaves $\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ij}$, the derivative and trace terms shown below; mixed components vanish because the metric blocks are independent of $t,\phi$. Thus the signed curvature formula [F5], contracted by $\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=R^a{}_{bad}$ from [F4], gives $$\operatorname{Ric}_{\alpha\beta}=-\frac1{2S}\partial_i\!\left(S h^{ij}\partial_jG_{\alpha\beta}\right)+\frac12h^{ij}\left(\partial_iG\,G^{-1}\partial_jG\right)_{\alpha\beta},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{\alpha i}=0,$$ $$\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ij}-\partial_iW_j+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}W_k-\frac14\operatorname{tr}(P_iP_j).$$ Here $\det G=-Dq$ and $\det h=S^2/(Dq)$, so the volume factor in the first formula is $\sqrt{|\det G\det h|}=S$. For the base block, substitution of the six coefficients in step 2.1 gives $$\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ij}=\frac{Mr(3a^2u^2-r^2)}{S^3}h_{ij}.$$ The remaining base terms cancel componentwise. For $(i,j)=(r,r)$, put $P_{rr}=M^2a^2u^2+3M^2r^2-2Ma^2ru^2-Ma^2r-3Mr^3+a^2r^2u^2+r^4$ and $Q_{rr}=M^2a^4u^4-2M^2a^2r^2u^2+5M^2r^4-2Ma^4ru^4+2Ma^4ru^2-2Ma^2r^3u^2-2Ma^2r^3-4Mr^5+a^4r^2u^4+2a^2r^4u^2+r^6$. The common numerator of $\operatorname{Ric}_{rr}$ over $S^2D^2$ is $Mr(3a^2u^2-r^2)D+SP_{rr}-Q_{rr}=0$. For $(r,u)$, the Hessian and trace terms are respectively $-uB/((u^2-1)SD)$ and $uB/((u^2-1)SD)$, where $B=-Ma^2u^2+Ma^2-2Mr^2+a^2ru^2+r^3$, and $\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ru}=0$. For $(u,u)$, put $P_{uu}=-Mru^2+Mr+a^2u^4+r^2u^2$ and $Q_{uu}=u^2(-4Ma^2ru^2+4Ma^2r+a^4u^4+2a^2r^2u^2+r^4)$. The common numerator of $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}$ over $q^2S^2$ is $Mr(3a^2u^2-r^2)q+P_{uu}qS-Q_{uu}=0$. Each polynomial identity follows by expanding $S=r^2+a^2u^2$, $D=r^2-2Mr+a^2$, and $q=1-u^2$; the signed formula retains both derivative and both quadratic-connection contributions.

In the fiber block, insert the explicit matrices $G,G^{-1},h^{-1}$ from step 1.1 into the first formula of step 3.1. Its three independent entries reduce to $$\operatorname{Ric}_{tt}=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{t\phi}=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{\phi\phi}=0.$$ This is the full $2\times2$ fiber block; the remaining three base entries vanish by the component cancellations in step 3.1 and the two mixed entries vanish by that formula. Hence the entire polar-chart Ricci matrix is zero, with no scalar-curvature shortcut.

The polar chart omits only the axis. By [A1] and [F2], $g$ is smooth there, and [F4]-[F5] make $\operatorname{Ric}(g)$ a smooth tensor. Since its components vanish on the dense axis-avoiding set by step 4.1, continuity makes $\operatorname{Ric}(g)$ vanish on the axis as well.
Thus $\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0$ at every point with $r>r_+$. The calculation proves a tensor identity for this specified metric; no Einstein field equation or classification of other metrics was used.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
