citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**The scope is exactly the continuous case, and that is not a limitation of the
proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

For $a>0$, the function $x\mapsto a^x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and
$$(a^x)'=a^x\log a.$$
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, with
$$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}.$$

Let $k\in\mathbb N$. Finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps is $C^k$. Scalar multiples are included among the finite componentwise operations. The assertions remain valid on an empty open domain.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Put $A=r^2+a^2$ and $q=\sin^2\theta$. The determinant of the $t,\phi$ block from [F1] is $-\Delta q$. On the stated smooth chart $q>0$ and [F2] gives $\Delta>0$, so this block is invertible; the smooth Lorentzian chart convention uses [A1].

Inverting the block from step 1.1 and using the diagonal $r,\theta$ entries gives $\Sigma g^{tt}=-A^2/\Delta+a^2q$, $\Sigma g^{t\phi}=-a(A/\Delta-1)$, $\Sigma g^{\phi\phi}=1/q-a^2/\Delta$, $g^{rr}=\Delta/\Sigma$, and $g^{\theta\theta}=1/\Sigma$. Direct multiplication with the covariant block verifies these entries as required by [F3].

For the separated ansatz, $\partial_tS=-E$, $\partial_\phi S=L$, $\partial_rS=S_r'$, and $\partial_\theta S=S_\theta'$. Substituting these derivatives and the inverse entries of step 2.1 into the equation in the Statement, then multiplying by $\Sigma$, yields $\Delta(S_r')^2-\frac{[E(r^2+a^2)-aL]^2}{\Delta}+\mu^2r^2+(S_\theta')^2+(L/\sin\theta-aE\sin\theta)^2+\mu^2a^2\cos^2\theta=0$.

The angular identity $(S_\theta')^2+(L/\sin\theta-aE\sin\theta)^2+\mu^2a^2\cos^2\theta=\Theta(\theta)+(L-aE)^2$ follows by expanding the square and using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$. The equation obtained in step 3.1 therefore separates into $\Delta^2(S_r')^2=\mathcal R(r)$ and $(S_\theta')^2=\Theta(\theta)$, with the $\mathcal R,\Theta$ of the Statement.

On the stated intervals the nonnegative square roots are continuous. Choose either sign on each interval and take primitives of $\sqrt{\mathcal R}/\Delta$ and $\sqrt{\Theta}$ using [F4]; since [F2] gives $\Delta>0$, the radial integrand is continuous. The resulting $S$ is $C^1$ and satisfies the two separated equations of step 4.1, hence satisfies the Hamilton-Jacobi equation by reversing that algebra.

Where the radicands are strictly positive, repeated use of the derivative formula in [F5] shows the square-root compositions have derivatives of every order; [F6] then gives smooth integrands, and their primitives are smooth because their first derivatives are smooth.
Thus the separated form is a local solution under the stated radicand conditions. The argument makes no claim across a zero of either radicand or about global geodesic completeness.

boundaries.reason: The statement assumes coordinate intervals and makes no empty-domain solution claim.

boundaries.evidence: Step 5.1 permits zero radicands and obtains C1 primitives; only smoothness is restricted to strictly positive radicands.

boundaries.reason: The equation is a local PDE on a four-coordinate rectangle and has no one-element case.

boundaries.evidence: Step 5.1 explicitly includes turning points as zero radicands for C1 solutions and excludes only a smoothness claim there.

boundaries.reason: The radial and angular intervals are open subintervals of the stated exterior polar chart; endpoints are not included.
The primitive construction fixes a base point on each stated interval and makes no family-selection claim.
The theorem gives sufficient radicand conditions for separated solutions, not an iff classification.
No converse that every solution separates is asserted.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**The scope is exactly the continuous case, and that is not a limitation of the
proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
This item fixes the unit and coordinate readings of the explicitly defined
Lorentzian objects, smooth-curve proper time and four-velocity of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], the tensor fields of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and the constructed connection,
curvature, Ricci and scalar fields of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]].
It states conventions, not a physical law or a measurement.

**(a) Constants and tensor slot.** Adopt $c>0$ with SI dimension
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, $G_N>0$ with dimension
$\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, and a signed parameter
$\Lambda$ with dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. No numerical value is asserted.
Define $\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, of dimension
$\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^2$.
For a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $T$ adopt the convention that its
components $T_{AB}=T(e_A,e_B)$ in an ordered $g$-orthonormal basis are energy
per volume, $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$.
This is a tensor slot and unit convention; interpreting a particular $T$ as
matter is a subsequent definition. Therefore $\kappa T_{AB}$ has dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$. No positivity, conservation or matter realization is assumed.

**(b) Coordinates and dimensions.** In a length-coordinate chart,
$x^0=ct$ and all four coordinates have units $\mathrm m$; $g_{ab}$ are
dimensionless and the quadratic line element $ds^2=g_{ab}dx^adx^b$ has units
$\mathrm m^2$. The Christoffel symbols defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) have units
$\mathrm m^{-1}$: the constructed formula differentiates dimensionless
$g_{ab}$ once with respect to a length coordinate. Curvature components have
units $\mathrm m^{-2}$ since the curvature operator differentiates the
connection once more and includes products of two connection coefficients;
so do $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ and scalar curvature $S$ in these coordinates.
In a time-coordinate chart $x^0=t$ has units $\mathrm s$, and $g_{00}$ has
units $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$; mixed, spatial, angular or other chart
components have the dimensions obtained by the coordinate Jacobians. A single
component has no universal dimension in a general chart. Orthonormal-frame
readings use the normalized geometric basis, with its length normalization.

**(c) Curves and invariant readings.** For the smooth future timelike curve
and positive scaling parameter of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] (e),
read $c$ as in (a) and
$\tau(s)=\tau_0+c^{-1}\int_{s_0}^{s}\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}\,dr$
as a proper-time parameter in seconds. Its four-velocity $U=d\gamma/d\tau$
has length-coordinate and normalized orthonormal components in
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; in a time-coordinate chart $U^0=dt/d\tau$
is dimensionless and other component dimensions follow the coordinates.
Lorentzian length $c\,\Delta\tau$ is in metres. The tensors $R^g$,
$\operatorname{Ric}$ and the scalar $S$ have the orthonormal readings
$\mathrm m^{-2}$, whereas the lowered curvature components in a mixed chart
have the units required by the metric and coordinate slots.

**(d) Future observer readings and SI restoration.** Let $n$ be a future
unit timelike vector, $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$. Define
$\rho_n:=T(n,n)$, $j_n:=-\sharp(T(n,\cdot))$ and its spatial part
$\phi_n:=j_n-\rho_n n$; indeed $g(j_n,n)=-\rho_n$, so
$g(\phi_n,n)=0$. In a $g$-orthonormal basis with $e_0=n$, set
$\phi^i=-T(e_0,e_i)=T^{0i}$ for $i=1,2,3$. The **SI energy flux** vector
and **SI momentum density** covector are, respectively,

$$q_n:=c\phi_n,\qquad p_n:=\phi_n^{\flat}/c,\qquad q_n^i=-cT_{0i},\qquad (p_n)_i=-T_{0i}/c.$$

Thus $\rho_n$ and each $\phi^i$ have units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$;
$q_n^i$ has units $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $(p_n)_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$. Stress components $T_{ij}$ have
units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{Pa}$. Tensor components retain the
common energy-density units; the factors of $c$ convert their mixed readings
to different SI quantities. Future-directedness and the signs here are part
of the convention, not positivity assumptions on $T$.

**(e) Natural units.** Setting $c=1$, or additionally $G_N=1$, abbreviates
these dimensionful conventions. Restore the factors displayed above before
comparison with SI quantities; in particular the same spatial tensor component
corresponds to energy flux multiplied by $c$ and momentum density divided by
$c$. In a chart whose coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ are all lengths and whose
metric components are $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, a nonzero null tangent
vector $v=(v^0,\mathbf v)$, null as in clause (b) of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], satisfies
$\|\mathbf v\|_2:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}=|v^0|$. Since $v\ne0$, this
implies $v^0\ne0$, so $\|\mathbf v\|_2/|v^0|=1$. This is a coordinate identity
for the null condition, not a postulate about light propagation, and it does
not change the physical constant $c$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

This item assumes the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through
the tangent-bundle structure used by
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)
([[def-countable-choice]]); no further choice principle is used.

**(a) Parameters and the Schwarzschild radius.** Let $c>0$ and $G_N>0$ be real
constants and let $m_*>0$ be a real **mass parameter**. Put

$$s:=\frac{2G_Nm_*}{c^2}>0 .$$

The number $s$ is the **Schwarzschild radius** of the datum. Neither $c$,
$G_N$ nor $m_*$ is measured here; the physical reading of $c$ and $G_N$ as the
framework's conversion and Newton constants and of $m_*$ as a mass is fixed by
the physical conventions of the framework, not by this definition.

**(b) The underlying manifold and its product charts.** Let $S^2:=S_2(0,1)=
\{y\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert y\rVert_2=1\}$ be the unit Euclidean sphere with the
subspace topology of [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]. Specify its
smooth structure as the maximal atlas generated by the following two charts
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). For $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$ put
$p_\varepsilon=(0,0,\varepsilon)$ and
$U_\varepsilon=S^2\setminus\{p_\varepsilon\}$, and define

$$\sigma_\varepsilon:U_\varepsilon\to\mathbb R^2,\qquad \sigma_\varepsilon(y)=\frac{(y_1,y_2)}{1-\varepsilon y_3}.$$

These open domains cover $S^2$. Each chart is a homeomorphism onto
$\mathbb R^2$, with inverse, for $u=(u_1,u_2)$ and $q=u_1^2+u_2^2$,

$$\sigma_\varepsilon^{-1}(u)=\left(\frac{2u_1}{1+q},\frac{2u_2}{1+q},\varepsilon\frac{q-1}{1+q}\right).$$

The two inverse identities follow by substitution; all displayed denominators
are nonzero on their domains. On the overlap both transition maps are
$u\mapsto u/(u_1^2+u_2^2)$ on $\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$, hence smooth.
The subspace is Hausdorff and has a countable basis given by intersections
with Euclidean balls of rational centres and positive rational radii.
Thus these charts specify a smooth two-manifold without boundary. This is
the standard sphere structure used for the round metric below: the inclusion
has the displayed smooth local parametrizations, and their differentials
are injective because composition with $\sigma_\varepsilon$ is the identity.
Let $M$ be the product manifold

$$M:=\mathbb R\times(s,\infty)\times S^2$$

with the product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]);
it is a smooth four-manifold without boundary. Write $x^0:M\to\mathbb R$ and
$r:M\to(s,\infty)$ for the first and second projections and $\iota:M\to S^2$
for the third. A **product chart** of $M$ is a smooth chart on the product
whose angular part is a smooth chart of $S^2$. In a **spherical-polar product
chart**, $0<\vartheta<\pi$ and the components of the round metric
$\gamma_{S^2}$ of [[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]
are $\gamma_{22}=1$, $\gamma_{23}=\gamma_{32}=0$,
$\gamma_{33}=\sin^2\vartheta$. These polar charts omit the two poles; ordinary
smooth sphere charts around the poles complete the product atlas.

**(c) The metric.** Let $f:(s,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be the smooth function

$$f(r):=1-\frac{s}{r} .$$

Define $g$ globally by the coordinate-free expression

$$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$

In every spherical-polar product chart its component functions are

$$g_{00}:=-f(r),\qquad g_{11}:=\frac{1}{f(r)},\qquad g_{22}:=r^2,\qquad g_{33}:=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,$$

and $g_{ab}:=0$ whenever $a\ne b$, $a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, with the index order
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$. This is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field on all of $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the component display is local
to spherical-polar charts, and $f>0$ because $r>s$. The pair $(M,g)$ is the **Schwarzschild exterior
metric of mass parameter $m_*$**; the datum of this definition is the
quadruple $(c,G_N,m_*,g)$. With these parameters fixed, write $(M,g,N)$
for its associated geometric datum, with $N$ as in clause (d). The geometric
datum depends on the parameters only through $s$ and does not retain $c$,
$G_N$ and $m_*$ separately. That $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is not asserted here; it is proved in the companion metric-properties lemma of this page (its
justification record in the frontmatter), which also records the equivalent
coordinate-free description
$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}$.

**(d) Time orientation and the Schwarzschild chart.** The field
$N:=\partial_0$ is the smooth product vector field on $M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); the chart components of $g$
are independent of $x^0$, so $N$ is the restriction of a global vector field,
and $g(N,N)=-f(r)<0$ at every point. The datum carries the time orientation
$N$. Spherical-polar product charts are **Schwarzschild charts** of the datum;
at the poles the same metric is represented in the smooth sphere charts of
the product atlas. We write $t$ for the coordinate $x^0/c$ when the datum is
read in the framework's unit conventions.

**(e) Scope.** The domain of the datum is the exterior region $r>s$; the
definition asserts nothing about $r=s$, about $r\le 0$, about any matter, or
about any equation satisfied by $g$. The horizon $r=s$ is not part of the
datum, and a continuation of the metric to $r=s$ requires the separate constructions recorded on this page, the
regularity lemma for the advanced chart and the Kruskal model-properties
lemma. Whether the datum is a solution of the
framework's field law is proved, not defined, in the Ricci-and-Einstein-tensor lemma of this
page.

Let $T=\partial_t$ be the stationary field and let $\Phi$ be the sphere
rotation field, extended to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$. Both are Killing fields.
In a smooth ingoing extension across $r=r_+$, the hypersurface $H^+=\{r=r_+\}$
is null and its null normal direction is generated by
$\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, where
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. On the exterior polar chart, $T$ is spacelike
exactly for

$$r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta),\qquad r_{\mathrm s}(\theta):=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$

At the rotation axis $r_{\mathrm s}=r_+$, so the open ergoregion has zero
radial width there.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with
its metric-selected connection $\nabla$. A smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K_{ab}$ is a **rank-two Killing tensor** when

$$\nabla_{(a}K_{bc)}:=\frac13\left(\nabla_aK_{bc}+\nabla_bK_{ca}+\nabla_cK_{ab}\right)=0.$$

For a smooth curve $\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ with open interval domain and affine
parameter $\lambda$, write $v=\dot\gamma$. If $\nabla_vv=0$, the curve is an
affinely parametrized geodesic, and $K_{ab}v^av^b$ is its associated quadratic
geodesic integral. It is called **reducible** if it is a finite constant
linear combination of $g_{ab}$ and symmetric products
$\xi^\flat\odot\eta^\flat$, where $\xi,\eta$ are Killing fields,
$\xi^\flat:=g(\xi,\cdot)$, and
$\alpha\odot\beta:=(\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha)/2$.

Let $K_{ab}$ be a smooth rank-two Killing tensor on a smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. If
$\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ is an affinely parametrized geodesic on a connected
open interval $I$, with tangent $v=\dot\gamma$, then

$$\lambda\longmapsto K_{ab}(\gamma(\lambda))v^a(\lambda)v^b(\lambda)$$

is constant on $I$.

For the specified Kerr exterior metric $g$, with $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and
$r>r_+$, the Ricci tensor of its metric-selected connection vanishes:
$\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0$. This is a local geometric identity on the entire
subextremal exterior, including the rotation axis by smooth extension.

On an axis-avoiding Kerr exterior coordinate
rectangle $I_t\times I_r\times I_\theta\times I_\phi$, with
$I_r\subset(r_+,\infty)$ and $I_\theta\subset(0,\pi)$, define the
geodesic Hamilton-Jacobi equation for a $C^1$ scalar $S$ by

$$g^{ab}\partial_aS\,\partial_bS=-\mu^2.$$

For constants $E,L,\mu,Q\in\mathbb R$, set

$$\mathcal R(r):=[E(r^2+a^2)-aL]^2-\Delta[\mu^2r^2+(L-aE)^2+Q],\qquad \Theta(\theta):=Q-\cos^2\theta\left[a^2(\mu^2-E^2)+\frac{L^2}{\sin^2\theta}\right].$$

If $\mathcal R\ge0$ on $I_r$ and $\Theta\ge0$ on $I_\theta$, then local
separated $C^1$ solutions are given by

$$S=-Et+L\phi+S_r(r)+S_\theta(\theta),\qquad S_r'=\pm\frac{\sqrt{\mathcal R}}{\Delta},\qquad S_\theta'=\pm\sqrt{\Theta}.$$

Where both radicands are strictly positive the branches are smooth. No
smoothness at a turning point or global continuation of a branch is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto

symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then

flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
This item assumes the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through
the tangent-bundle structure used by
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)
([[def-countable-choice]]); no further choice principle is used.

**(a) Parameters and the Schwarzschild radius.** Let $c>0$ and $G_N>0$ be real
constants and let $m_*>0$ be a real **mass parameter**. Put

$$s:=\frac{2G_Nm_*}{c^2}>0 .$$

The number $s$ is the **Schwarzschild radius** of the datum. Neither $c$,
$G_N$ nor $m_*$ is measured here; the physical reading of $c$ and $G_N$ as the
framework's conversion and Newton constants and of $m_*$ as a mass is fixed by
the physical conventions of the framework, not by this definition.

**(b) The underlying manifold and its product charts.** Let $S^2:=S_2(0,1)=
\{y\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert y\rVert_2=1\}$ be the unit Euclidean sphere with the
subspace topology of [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]. Specify its
smooth structure as the maximal atlas generated by the following two charts
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). For $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$ put
$p_\varepsilon=(0,0,\varepsilon)$ and
$U_\varepsilon=S^2\setminus\{p_\varepsilon\}$, and define

$$\sigma_\varepsilon:U_\varepsilon\to\mathbb R^2,\qquad \sigma_\varepsilon(y)=\frac{(y_1,y_2)}{1-\varepsilon y_3}.$$

These open domains cover $S^2$. Each chart is a homeomorphism onto
$\mathbb R^2$, with inverse, for $u=(u_1,u_2)$ and $q=u_1^2+u_2^2$,

$$\sigma_\varepsilon^{-1}(u)=\left(\frac{2u_1}{1+q},\frac{2u_2}{1+q},\varepsilon\frac{q-1}{1+q}\right).$$

The two inverse identities follow by substitution; all displayed denominators
are nonzero on their domains. On the overlap both transition maps are
$u\mapsto u/(u_1^2+u_2^2)$ on $\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$, hence smooth.
The subspace is Hausdorff and has a countable basis given by intersections
with Euclidean balls of rational centres and positive rational radii.
Thus these charts specify a smooth two-manifold without boundary. This is
the standard sphere structure used for the round metric below: the inclusion
has the displayed smooth local parametrizations, and their differentials
are injective because composition with $\sigma_\varepsilon$ is the identity.
Let $M$ be the product manifold

$$M:=\mathbb R\times(s,\infty)\times S^2$$

with the product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]);
it is a smooth four-manifold without boundary. Write $x^0:M\to\mathbb R$ and
$r:M\to(s,\infty)$ for the first and second projections and $\iota:M\to S^2$
for the third. A **product chart** of $M$ is a smooth chart on the product
whose angular part is a smooth chart of $S^2$. In a **spherical-polar product
chart**, $0<\vartheta<\pi$ and the components of the round metric
$\gamma_{S^2}$ of [[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]
are $\gamma_{22}=1$, $\gamma_{23}=\gamma_{32}=0$,
$\gamma_{33}=\sin^2\vartheta$. These polar charts omit the two poles; ordinary
smooth sphere charts around the poles complete the product atlas.

**(c) The metric.** Let $f:(s,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be the smooth function

$$f(r):=1-\frac{s}{r} .$$

Define $g$ globally by the coordinate-free expression

$$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}.$$

In every spherical-polar product chart its component functions are

$$g_{00}:=-f(r),\qquad g_{11}:=\frac{1}{f(r)},\qquad g_{22}:=r^2,\qquad g_{33}:=r^2\sin^2\vartheta,$$

and $g_{ab}:=0$ whenever $a\ne b$, $a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, with the index order
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$. This is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field on all of $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the component display is local
to spherical-polar charts, and $f>0$ because $r>s$. The pair $(M,g)$ is the **Schwarzschild exterior
metric of mass parameter $m_*$**; the datum of this definition is the
quadruple $(c,G_N,m_*,g)$. With these parameters fixed, write $(M,g,N)$
for its associated geometric datum, with $N$ as in clause (d). The geometric
datum depends on the parameters only through $s$ and does not retain $c$,
$G_N$ and $m_*$ separately. That $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is not asserted here; it is proved in the companion metric-properties lemma of this page (its
justification record in the frontmatter), which also records the equivalent
coordinate-free description
$g=-f\,d(x^0)\otimes d(x^0)+f^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\,\iota^*\gamma_{S^2}$.

**(d) Time orientation and the Schwarzschild chart.** The field
$N:=\partial_0$ is the smooth product vector field on $M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); the chart components of $g$
are independent of $x^0$, so $N$ is the restriction of a global vector field,
and $g(N,N)=-f(r)<0$ at every point. The datum carries the time orientation
$N$. Spherical-polar product charts are **Schwarzschild charts** of the datum;
at the poles the same metric is represented in the smooth sphere charts of
the product atlas. We write $t$ for the coordinate $x^0/c$ when the datum is
read in the framework's unit conventions.

**(e) Scope.** The domain of the datum is the exterior region $r>s$; the
definition asserts nothing about $r=s$, about $r\le 0$, about any matter, or
about any equation satisfied by $g$. The horizon $r=s$ is not part of the
datum, and a continuation of the metric to $r=s$ requires the separate constructions recorded on this page, the
regularity lemma for the advanced chart and the Kruskal model-properties
lemma. Whether the datum is a solution of the
framework's field law is proved, not defined, in the Ricci-and-Einstein-tensor lemma of this
page.

Let $T=\partial_t$ be the stationary field and let $\Phi$ be the sphere
rotation field, extended to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$. Both are Killing fields.
In a smooth ingoing extension across $r=r_+$, the hypersurface $H^+=\{r=r_+\}$
is null and its null normal direction is generated by
$\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, where
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. On the exterior polar chart, $T$ is spacelike
exactly for

$$r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta),\qquad r_{\mathrm s}(\theta):=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$

At the rotation axis $r_{\mathrm s}=r_+$, so the open ergoregion has zero
radial width there.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with
its metric-selected connection $\nabla$. A smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K_{ab}$ is a **rank-two Killing tensor** when

$$\nabla_{(a}K_{bc)}:=\frac13\left(\nabla_aK_{bc}+\nabla_bK_{ca}+\nabla_cK_{ab}\right)=0.$$

For a smooth curve $\gamma:I\to\mathcal M$ with open interval domain and affine
parameter $\lambda$, write $v=\dot\gamma$. If $\nabla_vv=0$, the curve is an
affinely parametrized geodesic, and $K_{ab}v^av^b$ is its associated quadratic
geodesic integral. It is called **reducible** if it is a finite constant
linear combination of $g_{ab}$ and symmetric products
$\xi^\flat\odot\eta^\flat$, where $\xi,\eta$ are Killing fields,
$\xi^\flat:=g(\xi,\cdot)$, and
$\alpha\odot\beta:=(\alpha\otimes\beta+\beta\otimes\alpha)/2$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
On an axis-avoiding Kerr exterior coordinate
rectangle $I_t\times I_r\times I_\theta\times I_\phi$, with
$I_r\subset(r_+,\infty)$ and $I_\theta\subset(0,\pi)$, define the
geodesic Hamilton-Jacobi equation for a $C^1$ scalar $S$ by

$$g^{ab}\partial_aS\,\partial_bS=-\mu^2.$$

For constants $E,L,\mu,Q\in\mathbb R$, set

$$\mathcal R(r):=[E(r^2+a^2)-aL]^2-\Delta[\mu^2r^2+(L-aE)^2+Q],\qquad \Theta(\theta):=Q-\cos^2\theta\left[a^2(\mu^2-E^2)+\frac{L^2}{\sin^2\theta}\right].$$

If $\mathcal R\ge0$ on $I_r$ and $\Theta\ge0$ on $I_\theta$, then local
separated $C^1$ solutions are given by

$$S=-Et+L\phi+S_r(r)+S_\theta(\theta),\qquad S_r'=\pm\frac{\sqrt{\mathcal R}}{\Delta},\qquad S_\theta'=\pm\sqrt{\Theta}.$$

Where both radicands are strictly positive the branches are smooth. No
smoothness at a turning point or global continuation of a branch is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

citations.quote:
Let $T=\partial_t$ be the stationary field and let $\Phi$ be the sphere
rotation field, extended to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$. Both are Killing fields.
In a smooth ingoing extension across $r=r_+$, the hypersurface $H^+=\{r=r_+\}$
is null and its null normal direction is generated by
$\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, where
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. On the exterior polar chart, $T$ is spacelike
exactly for

$$r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta),\qquad r_{\mathrm s}(\theta):=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$

At the rotation axis $r_{\mathrm s}=r_+$, so the open ergoregion has zero
radial width there.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq\mathcal M$ be open, let $S_{ab}$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $U$, and let $X$ be a smooth Killing field on $U$. For
$X_b:=g_{bc}X^c$ and $S^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}S_{cd}$, define the
**Killing-multiplier current** by

$$j_X^a:=-S^{ab}X_b.$$

At a point $p\in U$ and for an observer $n\in T_p\mathcal M$ with
$g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ future-directed, define the associated
**Killing-multiplier density** by

$$\rho_X(p;n):=-g_p(n,j_X)=S_{ab}(p)n^aX^b.$$

The current and density are defined for every such $S,X,n$. The definition
imposes no conservation equation, sign condition, or coercivity property.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be a scalar-field
matter model on $M$ with action differences $\Delta S$, scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor $T$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Matter first variation.** Let $u\mapsto\varphi_u$, $|u|<u_0$, be a family
of smooth functions with $\varphi_{u=0}=\varphi$ such that $(\varphi_u-\varphi)$ is supported in a fixed
compact set for all $u$ and the functions $(u,p)\mapsto\varphi_u(p)$ are
smooth. Then $u\mapsto\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)$ is differentiable at $0$ and

$$\frac{d}{du}\Big|_{u=0}\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)=\frac{K}{c}\int_M\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\,\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta\varphi:=\partial_u\varphi_u|_{u=0}.$$

In particular the family is stationary in this direction, for every such
family, exactly when $\Box_g\varphi=V'(\varphi)$.

**(b) Metric variation and Hilbert tensor.** Let $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<s_0$, be
a smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly supported variation, and let
$q^{ab}=\partial_sg_s^{ab}|_{s=0}$. Then

$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\Delta S(\varphi,g_s)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently $T$ is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field model
at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]), and by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]] it is the only one.

**(c) Conservation identity.** On $M$,

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=K\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\partial_b\varphi .$$

Consequently the scalar equation implies $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$. Conversely conservation implies the scalar equation at each point where $d\varphi\ne0$, and therefore everywhere if that set is dense, by continuity. No converse follows on an open constant-field region.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Because $T$ is spacelike by [F1], decompose it relative to $n$ as $T=\alpha n+w$, where $\alpha:=-g(T,n)$ and $w:=T+g(T,n)n\in n^\perp$. By [F2], if $\beta:=\sqrt{g(w,w)}$ then $\beta>|\alpha|$; set $e:=w/\beta$, so $g(e,e)=1$, $g(n,e)=0$, and $T=\alpha n+\beta e$.

Set $\lambda:=-(n^\flat+e^\flat)$ at $p$, where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$ and $e^\flat=g(e,\cdot)$. Then $\lambda(n)=1$, $\lambda(e)=-1$, and $\lambda$ vanishes on the orthogonal complement of $\operatorname{span}\{n,e\}$. In a smooth chart, the local function $\varphi(x)=\lambda_a(x^a-x^a(p))$ has $d\varphi_p=\lambda$. Thus $g^{-1}(\lambda,\lambda)=-1+1=0$ and $\lambda(T)=\alpha-\beta$.

By [F3], at $p$ the scalar stress tensor is $Q_{ab}=K(\lambda_a\lambda_b-\frac12g_{ab}g^{-1}(\lambda,\lambda))$. Using [F4] and $g^{-1}(\lambda,\lambda)=0$, $\rho_T(p;n)=Q_{ab}n^aT^b=K\lambda(n)\lambda(T)=K(\alpha-\beta)<0$. Hence the stationary Killing-multiplier density is not nonnegative on all smooth scalar first-derivative data at $p$.

For any field that additionally satisfies $\Box_g\varphi=0$, [F5] makes $Q$ divergence-free and [F6] makes the associated Killing current divergence-free. This is conditional; the example does not assert existence of an on-shell solution with the selected first derivative. Step 3.1 proves that the local density form itself is indefinite, so this multiplier alone does not provide a pointwise nonnegative coercive density on a region containing $p$.

boundaries.reason: The example assumes a point strictly inside the open ergoregion.
The density conclusion is strictly negative when T is spacelike; the zero-density stationary-limit boundary is excluded by the hypothesis.
No cardinality-one case is involved.
The null boundary where T ceases to be spacelike is excluded; the proof uses beta>|alpha|.
The example assumes an exterior point in the open ergoregion, not its horizon, axis, or stationary-limit boundary.
The first-jet witness is constructed in a chart and uses no choice from a nonempty family.
The example establishes a sign counterexample, not an equivalence.

The explicit local scalar derivative gives negative stationary density in an ergoregion; the result is not a converse classification of energy conditions or a global wave-existence theorem. This public claim is not a biconditional requiring a separate reverse implication.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $T=\partial_t$ be the stationary field and let $\Phi$ be the sphere
rotation field, extended to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$. Both are Killing fields.
In a smooth ingoing extension across $r=r_+$, the hypersurface $H^+=\{r=r_+\}$
is null and its null normal direction is generated by
$\chi=T+\Omega_H\Phi$, where
$\Omega_H=a/(r_+^2+a^2)$. On the exterior polar chart, $T$ is spacelike
exactly for

$$r_+<r<r_{\mathrm s}(\theta),\qquad r_{\mathrm s}(\theta):=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$

At the rotation axis $r_{\mathrm s}=r_+$, so the open ergoregion has zero
radial width there.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq\mathcal M$ be open, let $S_{ab}$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $U$, and let $X$ be a smooth Killing field on $U$. For
$X_b:=g_{bc}X^c$ and $S^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}S_{cd}$, define the
**Killing-multiplier current** by

$$j_X^a:=-S^{ab}X_b.$$

At a point $p\in U$ and for an observer $n\in T_p\mathcal M$ with
$g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ future-directed, define the associated
**Killing-multiplier density** by

$$\rho_X(p;n):=-g_p(n,j_X)=S_{ab}(p)n^aX^b.$$

The current and density are defined for every such $S,X,n$. The definition
imposes no conservation equation, sign condition, or coercivity property.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be a scalar-field
matter model on $M$ with action differences $\Delta S$, scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor $T$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Matter first variation.** Let $u\mapsto\varphi_u$, $|u|<u_0$, be a family
of smooth functions with $\varphi_{u=0}=\varphi$ such that $(\varphi_u-\varphi)$ is supported in a fixed
compact set for all $u$ and the functions $(u,p)\mapsto\varphi_u(p)$ are
smooth. Then $u\mapsto\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)$ is differentiable at $0$ and

$$\frac{d}{du}\Big|_{u=0}\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)=\frac{K}{c}\int_M\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\,\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta\varphi:=\partial_u\varphi_u|_{u=0}.$$

In particular the family is stationary in this direction, for every such
family, exactly when $\Box_g\varphi=V'(\varphi)$.

**(b) Metric variation and Hilbert tensor.** Let $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<s_0$, be
a smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly supported variation, and let
$q^{ab}=\partial_sg_s^{ab}|_{s=0}$. Then

$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\Delta S(\varphi,g_s)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently $T$ is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field model
at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]), and by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]] it is the only one.

**(c) Conservation identity.** On $M$,

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=K\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\partial_b\varphi .$$

Consequently the scalar equation implies $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$. Conversely conservation implies the scalar equation at each point where $d\varphi\ne0$, and therefore everywhere if that set is dense, by continuity. No converse follows on an open constant-field region.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
  (invariance of the action under simultaneous pullback by the flow).

Then $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.consumer_use: 1.1: Because $T$ is spacelike by [F1], decompose it relative to $n$ as $T=\alpha n+w$, where $\alpha:=-g(T,n)$ and $w:=T+g(T,n)n\in n^\perp$. By [F2], if $\beta:=\sqrt{g(w,w)}$ then $\beta>|\alpha|$; set $e:=w/\beta$, so $g(e,e)=1$, $g(n,e)=0$, and $T=\alpha n+\beta e$.
